slot.brief: Simplify |z1 z2| / |z1| type expression or find a z satisfying a modulus equation using modulus-conjugate relations

stem: If a complex number \(z\) satisfies \(z + |z| = 2 + 8i\), then \(|z|\) equals
notes: from question bank g571ac13d94fe (verified in job 20261127-122012-292e)
working:
Let \(z = re^{i\theta}\) so \(|z|=r\). Then \(z+|z| = r(\cos\theta+1 + i\sin\theta) = 2+8i\).
Equate imaginary: \(r\sin\theta = 8\).
Equate real: \(r(\cos\theta+1) = 2 \Rightarrow r\cos\theta = 2-r\).
Square and add: \((r\sin\theta)^2 + (r\cos\theta)^2 = 8^2 + (2-r)^2\).
Left side is \(r^2\). Thus \(r^2 = 64 + 4 - 4r + r^2\).
Simplifying, \(68 - 4r = 0 \Rightarrow r = 17\).
Hence \(|z| = 17\).

Independent check: Let z=x+iy and r=|z|. Comparing imaginary parts gives y=8; real parts give x=2-r. Then r²=x²+64=(2-r)²+64, so r=17.
solution:
Let $z=x+iy$ and $r=|z|$. Equating real and imaginary parts gives $x=2-r$ and $y=8$.
$$r^2=x^2+y^2=(2-r)^2+64$$
Hence $4r=68$, so $|z|=r=17$.
